s2_1: First, let's understand what Fast Tag actually is.
s2_2: Fast Tag is a small R F I D sticker that is fixed on the vehicle's windshield.
s2_3: It links your vehicle to a prepaid wallet or a bank account.
s2_4: Its job is to pay the toll automatically, without stopping at the toll plaza.
s2_5: Fast Tag is part of the National Electronic Toll Collection, or N E T C, programme.
s2_6: The N E T C system was developed by N P C eye, the same N P C eye that runs U P eye.
s2_7: In India, Fast Tag was made mandatory for most vehicles from February twenty twenty-one.
s2_8: Queues got shorter, and the cash hassle went away.
s2_9: To get a Fast Tag, you need the vehicle's R C and K.Y.C. documents.
s3_1: Let's first understand the main parts of the Fast Tag system.
s3_2: First, the Fast Tag itself, with a unique Tag I D.
s3_3: Second is the toll plaza's R F I D reader and antenna, fixed above the lane.
s3_4: Third is the toll plaza's computer system, which handles the data of every lane.
s3_5: Fourth is the acquirer bank, the bank that collects payment on behalf of the toll plaza.
s3_6: Fifth is the issuer bank, the bank that issued your Fast Tag and holds your wallet.
s3_7: And between them all is N P C eye's N E T C system, which routes messages to the right bank.
s3_8: Different banks issue Fast Tags, but thanks to N E T C, your tag works at every Fast Tag toll plaza in India.
s4_1: Now the most interesting question. This small sticker has no battery, so how does it work?
s4_2: Fast Tag uses R F I D technology, which means Radio Frequency Identification.
s4_3: Inside the sticker there is a tiny chip, with a thin antenna around it.
s4_4: When the vehicle comes near the reader, the reader sends out radio waves.
s4_5: These radio waves give the tag's chip a little energy, and it becomes active.
s4_6: The tag then sends its unique I D back to the reader as a radio signal.
s4_7: This is called passive R F I D, so Fast Tag needs no battery or charging.
s4_8: Note that your money or bank details are not stored inside the tag.
s4_9: The tag only tells its I D; all the other work happens on the servers of the banks and the N E T C system.
s4_10: In India, Fast Tag works on a U H F radio frequency band, so the reader can read the tag from a few metres away.
s4_11: If the sticker gets bent or torn, its antenna can be damaged, and the reader may not be able to read it.
s5_1: Now let's see what actually happens at the toll plaza, step by step.
s5_2: Suppose your Fast Tag wallet has five hundred rupees, and the toll is ninety-five rupees.
s5_3: As soon as the car enters the Fast Tag lane, the reader reads the tag's I D.
s5_4: The toll plaza system uses this I D to check the tag's details and status.
s5_5: The plaza keeps an updated status list of tags, so the check can happen very quickly.
s5_6: If the tag is valid, the toll amount is set by the vehicle's class, and the barrier opens.
s5_7: Then the toll plaza sends the transaction to its acquirer bank.
s5_8: The acquirer bank passes this request to your issuer bank through N P C eye's N E T C system.
s5_9: The issuer bank debits ninety-five rupees from your Fast Tag wallet.
s5_10: After that, through settlement, the money reaches the toll plaza's account.
s5_11: And a debit S M S arrives on your phone.
s5_12: Note that the barrier can open immediately, but the debit S M S may sometimes come a little later.
s5_13: At many toll plazas, cameras also check the vehicle's number plate and class.
s5_14: And this whole process is usually completed in just a few seconds.
s6_1: Now the question is, how is the toll amount decided?
s6_2: Every Fast Tag is linked to a vehicle class, like car, light commercial vehicle, bus or truck.
s6_3: Every toll plaza has its own fee rate, which differs by vehicle class.
s6_4: That's why a truck pays more toll than a car.
s6_5: Many plazas may also offer options like return journey or monthly passes.
s6_6: If you are ever charged for the wrong class, you can complain to your issuer bank.
s6_7: Toll rates are updated from time to time, as per government rules.
s6_8: Every toll plaza's fee rate can be checked on N H A I's official website or app.
s7_1: Sometimes a vehicle gets stopped at the toll plaza even with a Fast Tag. Why?
s7_2: The most common reason is low balance.
s7_3: If the wallet doesn't have enough balance, the tag can go into low-balance or blacklist status.
s7_4: Incomplete K.Y.C., or vehicle details that don't match, can also be a reason.
s7_5: Under the One Vehicle One Fast Tag policy of N H A I, a vehicle should have only one active Fast Tag.
s7_6: Without a valid Fast Tag, you may have to pay more than the normal toll.
s7_7: So check your balance and tag status before a trip.
s7_8: After you recharge, the tag's status becomes active again within some time.
s8_1: Now, let's talk about recharging your Fast Tag.
s8_2: Most Fast Tags work like a prepaid wallet that you recharge in advance.
s8_3: You can recharge through the issuer bank's app, net banking, or U P eye payment apps.
s8_4: Some banks also give the option to link Fast Tag directly to your bank account.
s8_5: After a recharge, the balance can sometimes take a little time to update.
s8_6: So before a long journey, it's better to recharge a little in advance.
s8_7: Many banks also send an S M S alert when the balance is low.
s8_8: Some apps also have an auto-recharge option, which tops up the wallet as soon as the balance runs low.
